clue.text: Leave harbour on a bicycle?

definitions.meaning: a ship leaving port must cross the sandbar across the harbour mouth
the horizontal tube joining saddle post and handlebars on a bike frame

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the answer into two words: to get out of harbour, a vessel crosses the bar, the sandbank at its entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: The top tube of a man's bicycle frame is its crossbar; a sailing vessel leaving port passes over the bar at the harbour mouth.

clue.text: Blue bomb?

definitions.meaning: a deep blue pigment or colour
a nuclear weapon jacketed in a metal that leaves heavy radioactive fallout

explanation.definitionFit: Cobalt blue is a pigment shade, and a cobalt bomb is a hypothetical nuclear device salted with that metal.

clue.text: Monkey goes for most of the fruit

definitions.text: Monkey goes for most of the fruit

parts.words: Monkey goes for most of the fruit
parts.note: the orang, short for orang-utan, stands in for the fruit's name lacking only its final letter

explanation.surface: A monkey grabs most of the fruit for itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes for' means 'stands for': ORANG (an ape, loosely a monkey) spells all of the citrus fruit except its last letter, E.
explanation.definitionFit: A citrus fruit, whose name begins with the short form of the great ape's name.

clue.text: He may feel triumphant at saint's bedevilment

definitions.text: He may feel triumphant at saint's bedevilment

indicators.note: to bedevil is to throw into confusion, so the letters of the preceding words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A devil-worshipper gloats when a holy man is tormented.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signalled by 'bedevilment' uses AT and SAINTS (the S of the possessive counts here); the whole clue then describes a devil-worshipper relishing a saint's torment.
explanation.definitionFit: A worshipper of the Devil would rejoice at the torment of a holy person.

clue.text: Damaged oar going round pole in the river

indicators.note: going round means the rearranged letters surround the next piece
damaged things are broken up, so these three letters are rearranged

parts.note: N is short for the north pole

explanation.surface: A broken oar floats round a punting pole in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Damaged' rearranges OAR to ARO, and 'going round' places N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arno is the Italian waterway flowing through Florence and Pisa.

clue.text: Reduction in prices

parts.note: reads as a price cut, but means a shortened summary, whose letters are found rearranged in the word prices

explanation.surface: A shop announces a price cut.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a sale; 'reduction' is instead a cut-down summary of a text, and its six letters are those of PRICES rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A précis is a summary, a text reduced to its essentials.

clue.text: Cut out a part, in the theatre

definitions.text: Cut out a part, in the theatre

parts.words: Cut out a part, in the theatre
parts.note: sounds like an actor's role being axed, but the theatre is an operating theatre where a surgeon removes tissue

explanation.surface: A director drops a role from a stage production.
explanation.walkthrough: The theatre is the hospital operating theatre, not a playhouse, and the part is part of an organ.
explanation.definitionFit: To resect is to surgically remove a portion of an organ or bone.

clue.text: One type of fish following another, moving crabwise

indicators.note: following means the second fish is placed after the first

parts.note: craw is a short form of crawfish, a freshwater crustacean
the ling is a long North Atlantic food fish

explanation.surface: One kind of fish trails behind another, scuttling sideways like a crab.
explanation.walkthrough: Craw, a short form of crawfish (crayfish), counts as a fish here by its name. Crabs creep along the seabed, hence the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabs move by creeping slowly along the bottom on their legs.

clue.text: Dissipated peers die quicker

indicators.note: dissipated suggests dissolute lords but signals that the letters are scattered and reformed

explanation.surface: Dissolute lords die younger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dissipated' rearranges PEERS and DIE.
explanation.definitionFit: More speedy means faster, a comparative of quick.

clue.text: Showing off snake bite?

parts.note: a boa is a large constricting snake
a sting is an insect's bite or wound

explanation.surface: A snake's bite shown off as a trophy.
explanation.definitionFit: Bragging means talking in a way that shows off one's achievements.

clue.text: Country home dubious asset — out of the way, note

indicators.note: dubious means questionable or shaky, so the letters of the next word are rearranged
out of the way says one letter of the rearranged word is cleared aside

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A rural mansion is a doubtful investment best got rid of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of the way' drops one of the two Ss of ASSET, and 'dubious' rearranges the rest, ASET, to ESTA; TE is added. The clue leaves which letter goes unstated.
explanation.definitionFit: A large country house with its grounds and land is called an estate.

clue.text: House in which no-one would enjoy living

definitions.text: House in which no-one would enjoy living

parts.words: House in which no-one would enjoy living
parts.note: describes a building whose residents are all dead: a vault for bones

explanation.surface: An estate agent's warning about an unlovable property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Living' is the trap: nobody living there means the occupants are dead, as in a charnel house, a store for bones.
explanation.definitionFit: A charnel house is a vault where the bones of the dead are kept.

clue.text: Might it be the sole inscription on a coin?

definitions.text: Might it be the sole inscription on a coin?

parts.words: Might it be the sole inscription on a coin?
parts.note: split into two words it names the end of a leg, which is a foot's sole; whole, it is the lettering stamped round a coin

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a coin carries only one inscription.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sole' looks like 'only', but it is the underside of the foot, at the leg's end.
explanation.definitionFit: The wording around the rim of a coin or medal is called its legend.

clue.text: Expressed amusement seeing student thrown around

indicators.note: around means the thrown word goes about the student letter

parts.note: chucked means thrown or tossed
L is the learner plate letter, standing for a student

explanation.surface: Onlookers laughed to see a student tossed about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' puts L inside CHUCKED.
explanation.definitionFit: To laugh quietly is to show that something amuses you.

clue.text: Leaves to rub back and cut tail off

indicators.note: back says the word rub is read in the other direction

parts.note: to dock an animal is to cut its tail short

explanation.surface: Instructions to rub some leaves backwards and trim a tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns RUB into BUR. 'Leaves' stands for the plant itself, known for its broad leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Burdock is a weedy plant with huge leaves and hooked burrs, so it can be named by its foliage.

clue.text: Vagrant queries a gentleman's style

indicators.note: vagrant means wandering, so the letters of the next word wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A tramp asks about a gentleman's manners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vagrant' rearranges QUERIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Esq. after a man's name is a courtesy title, the formal style for a gentleman.

clue.text: Solo performance in the concert

indicators.note: in shows the answer sits inside the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A soloist takes a turn during the concert.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer lies in conCERT's opening letters after the C: c-ONCE-rt.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done a single time only, as a solo is performed by one person a single time.

clue.text: African tribesman is found in the shrubbery

parts.note: the Berbers are a people of North Africa
taken as written

explanation.surface: A North African tribesman turns up hiding among the bushes.
explanation.walkthrough: BERBER, of the North African people, plus IS gives the shrub, also called barberry.
explanation.definitionFit: Berberis, or barberry, is a thorny garden shrub planted in borders and hedges.

clue.text: Avoid being locked up because of this youth?

parts.note: to miss something is to avoid it
pent means penned or shut in

explanation.surface: A wasted youth could land you in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: MISS plus PENT gives the misspent youth that might lead to prison. The grid prints MISSPELT, but the wordplay and the phrase 'misspent youth' both need N.
explanation.definitionFit: A wasted youth is a misspent one, the stock phrase for years squandered.

clue.text: National and public schoolboy holding skin-head

indicators.note: holding means the schoolboy word contains the next piece

parts.note: an Etonian is a pupil of Eton, the famous English public school

indicators.note: head means the first letter of the word skin

explanation.surface: A public schoolboy hangs on to a shaven-headed youth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holding' puts S, the head of 'skin', inside ETONIAN. Eton is a fee-paying English boarding school, which Britons call a public school.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Estonia is one of its nationals.

clue.text: End of life, taking this and holding cross? Just so!

definitions.text: End of life, taking this and holding cross? Just so!

indicators.note: holding means the pieces before it contain the cross
end of picks the final letter of the word life

parts.note: it can stand for this, a thing just mentioned
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: Death is the final thing, taking up one's cross. Exactly so!
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of' takes E from life, IT follows, and 'holding' places X after the E. The whole clue also describes death, an exit from life.
explanation.definitionFit: A departure from life, death is often called one's final exit.

clue.text: Served a concoction with unfortunate result

indicators.note: a concoction is something mixed up, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A waiter served a strange dish, with unhappy consequences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concoction' rearranges SERVED A.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverse effects are harmful or unfavourable ones, turning out badly.

clue.text: In the galley, I'm befuddled with beer

indicators.note: befuddled means confused by drink, so the letters around it are jumbled

explanation.surface: A drunken rower admits he is fuddled with beer in the galley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Befuddled' rearranges IM and BEER. 'Galley' looks like a ship's kitchen but is the oared ship itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A bireme was an ancient galley with two banks of oars.

clue.text: Uncle Dicky and go to central masses

annotationWithheld.why: 'Uncle Dicky and go to central masses' as held: the anagram of UNCLE gives NUCLE, but no clue word supplies the final I (probably 'and I go to' with the I lost in transcription); no scan to confirm
annotationWithheld.clue: Uncle Dicky and go to central masses

clue.text: Frisk in the briny at pier-end, with companion

parts.note: the briny is a jokey name for the sea

indicators.note: end means the last letter of the word pier

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: Bathers frolic in the sea at the end of the pier with a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frisk' looks like frolic; it is the police sense, to search a person. R is the pier's end.
explanation.definitionFit: To pat someone down for hidden items is to search them.

clue.text: Tree cover for Mid-west mountain needing soil

indicators.note: cover for means the tree goes around the next pieces

parts.note: a birch is a slender tree with pale bark

indicators.note: mid picks out the middle letters of the word west

parts.note: M is an abbreviation for mountain on maps

explanation.surface: Trees shelter a mountain in the American Midwest that needs fresh earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mid' takes the two middle letters of 'west', and 'cover for' puts them and the mountain inside the tree. 'Soil' is the verb, not earth.
explanation.definitionFit: To dirty or sully, whether a surface or a reputation, is to besmirch it.

clue.text: Doctor expected to arrive carrying large piece of computer hardware

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor

indicators.note: carrying means the word for expected contains the next letter

parts.note: due means scheduled or expected
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A doctor is due, bringing a big new component for the computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carrying' puts the large letter inside the word for expected. The grid prints NODULE, but the wordplay and definition need M at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A module is a self-contained unit plugged into a larger system, as in a computer.

clue.text: Obliging lady giving us tea

definitions.meaning: a charwoman or cleaner, who obliges by doing housework
slang for a cup of tea, from Chinese cha

explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a char is a daily cleaning woman, once called 'a woman who obliges'; char is also old slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleaning woman is called a charlady, and British slang uses the same short word for a cuppa.

clue.text: On the rocks, about to come back for a jacket

parts.note: a reef is a ridge of rocks near the surface of the sea

indicators.note: to come back means the word for about is read backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Shipwrecked on the rocks, someone returns for a coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To come back' turns the two-letter word for about backwards. A reefer is also slang for a cannabis cigarette, but here it is the sailor's coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A reefer is a thick double-breasted jacket of the kind worn by sailors.

clue.text: Dramatic account of farmworker grabbing her, none-the-less

indicators.note: grabbing means the farmworker holds the next piece inside

parts.note: a tiller is someone who tills the soil

indicators.note: read as her with the E taken off, the clue's pun on nonetheless

explanation.surface: A thriller about a farmhand seizing a woman anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'None-the-less' is a pun on nonetheless, read as 'her' with an E removed; 'grabbing' puts what remains inside the farmworker.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspense novel or film is an exciting, dramatic story.

clue.text: Making arrangements for the dog?

definitions.meaning: one who sets things out or arranges them
a breed of gun dog, such as the red Irish breed

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a person who sets, arranges things, as a crossword compiler does.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who arranges things sets them, and a long-haired gun dog breed shares the name.

clue.text: Wave covering grain vessel

indicators.note: covering is a link that puts the grain before the vessel

parts.note: bran is the husk of cereal grain
a dish is a vessel for food

explanation.surface: Someone waves a bowl topped with cereal.
explanation.definitionFit: To flourish a weapon or object in the air is to wave it about.
